questions.q: What is the correct sequence of segments in the TCP three-way handshake?
questions.exp: The client sends SYN, the server replies SYN-ACK, and the client completes with ACK.

questions.q: A packet-filtering firewall makes its decisions mainly by examining
options: The full text of e-mail bodies
The physical condition of network cables
IP addresses and port numbers in packet headers
questions.exp: Packet filters inspect header fields such as source/destination IP address, port and protocol against rules.

Which of the following Python data types is NOT mutable?
questions.exp: Tuples are immutable sequences; lists, dictionaries and sets can be modified in place.

questions.q: Which statement about a constructor in C++ is correct?
options: It has the same name as its class and no return type
It must return an int value
questions.exp: A constructor carries the class name and has no return type (not even void); it cannot be static or virtual.

questions.q: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for routing packets from source host to destination host across networks?
questions.exp: The network layer handles logical addressing and routing of packets between networks.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a desirable characteristic of a good Software Requirements Specification (SRS)?
options: Containing detailed implementation and coding decisions
questions.exp: An SRS should state what the system must do, not how it is implemented; embedding design/coding decisions is undesirable.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
print(type(3/2), type(3//2))
questions.exp: The / operator always gives a float, while // on two ints gives an int.

questions.q: A line is drawn from (2, 3) to (8, 6) using the DDA algorithm. How many steps (iterations) will the algorithm take?
questions.exp: dx = 6, dy = 3; steps = max(|dx|, |dy|) = 6.

questions.q: A one-dimensional array A[-5..20] is stored in memory with base address 1000 and each element occupies 4 bytes. What is the address of A[8]?
Which of the following is NOT stored in the Process Control Block (PCB) of a process?
options: The complete source code of the program
The process state and process ID
questions.exp: The PCB holds execution context and bookkeeping information (PC, registers, state, PID, scheduling data), not the source code.

questions.q: Which of the following translates the whole source program into object code before execution begins?
questions.exp: A compiler translates the entire program in one go; an interpreter translates and executes statement by statement.

questions.q: If f(n) = 3n² + 5n + 2, which of the following is correct?
questions.exp: Dominant term is 3n², so f(n) is bounded above and below by constant multiples of n²: Θ(n²).

questions.q: Reference string: 1,2,3,4,1,2,5,1,2,3,4,5 with 3 frames and FIFO replacement. How many page faults occur?
questions.exp: Faults on 1,2,3,4,1,2,5,3,4 (the references to 1,2 after 5 and to 5 at the end are hits) = 9.

questions.q: Who is credited with writing the first algorithm meant to be executed on a machine, for Babbage's Analytical Engine?
questions.exp: Ada Lovelace's notes on the Analytical Engine contained an algorithm to compute Bernoulli numbers, regarded as the first program.

questions.q: Consider FCFS scheduling for processes P1 (arrival 0, burst 5), P2 (arrival 1, burst 3), P3 (arrival 2, burst 8). What is the average waiting time?
questions.exp: P1 starts at 0 (WT 0), P2 starts at 5 (WT 4), P3 starts at 8 (WT 6); average = 10/3 = 3.33.

questions.q: The Gray code equivalent of the binary number 1011 is
questions.exp: MSB stays 1; then 1⊕0 = 1, 0⊕1 = 1, 1⊕1 = 0, giving 1110.

questions.q: Equivalence class partitioning and boundary value analysis are techniques of which kind of testing?
questions.exp: Both derive test cases from the input domain and specification without looking at the internal code, so they are black-box techniques.

questions.q: Using a Caesar cipher with key 3, the plaintext CAT is encrypted as
questions.exp: Each letter shifts 3 places forward: C→F, A→D, T→W.

questions.q: The first web browser, written by Tim Berners-Lee in 1990, was named:
questions.exp: Berners-Lee's first browser/editor was called WorldWideWeb (later renamed Nexus).

questions.q: Simplify the Boolean expression A + A'B.
questions.exp: By the absorption (redundancy) law A + A'B = (A + A')(A + B) = A + B.

questions.q: Checking that the operands of an arithmetic operator have compatible types is the job of which compiler phase?
questions.exp: Type checking needs symbol-table information and is done in semantic analysis.

questions.q: How many swaps does bubble sort perform to sort the array 5 4 3 2 1 into ascending order?
questions.exp: Each swap removes exactly one inversion. The reversed array of 5 elements has 5×4/2 = 10 inversions, so 10 swaps.

questions.q: Encapsulation in OOP means:
options: Deriving a new class from an existing class
Using one name for many different forms
Showing only the essential features to the user
Binding data and the functions that operate on it into one unit and restricting direct access to the data
questions.exp: Encapsulation wraps data and methods together in a class and controls access to the data using access specifiers.

questions.q: A Unix-like inode has 10 direct pointers and 1 single-indirect pointer. Block size is 1 KB and a block pointer is 4 bytes. What is the maximum file size?
questions.exp: A single-indirect block holds 1024/4 = 256 pointers; total blocks = 10 + 256 = 266, so 266 KB.

questions.q: In C++, when a class is derived using private inheritance, the public members of the base class become ____ members of the derived class.
questions.exp: Private inheritance makes all accessible base members (public and protected) private in the derived class.

questions.q: GSM belongs to which generation of mobile networks?
questions.exp: GSM is a digital cellular standard of the second generation (2G).

questions.q: What is the main task of Pass 1 of a two-pass assembler?
options: Generate final object code with all operands resolved
Assign addresses to labels and build the symbol table
Resolve references to symbols in other modules
Relocate the program at load time
questions.exp: Pass 1 scans the source, maintains the location counter and records label addresses in the symbol table; code is generated in Pass 2.

questions.q: Evaluate the postfix expression: 5 6 2 + * 12 4 / -

questions.exp: 200 + 2×10 + 2×5 = 230px; margin is outside the box.

questions.q: Table Emp(id, sal) contains rows (1,100), (2,200), (3,NULL), (4,200). What does SELECT COUNT(sal), COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT sal) FROM Emp return?
questions.exp: COUNT(sal) ignores NULL giving 3; COUNT(*) counts all 4 rows; DISTINCT non-null sal values are 100 and 200, so 2.

questions.q: Google App Engine, which lets developers deploy their code without managing servers or operating systems, is best classified as:
questions.exp: It provides a platform (runtime and tools) for building applications, which is Platform as a Service.

questions.q: The Java compiler (javac) translates source code into:
options: Native machine code of the host CPU
Object code specific to the operating system
questions.exp: javac produces platform-independent bytecode (.class files), which the JVM interprets or JIT-compiles.

questions.q: Data bits 1101011 are to be sent using even parity. What should the parity bit be?
questions.exp: The data has five 1s (odd), so a parity bit of 1 makes the total number of 1s even.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
s = "programming"
print(s[2:8:2], s[::-3])

questions.q: Which file mode opens a file for both reading and writing and first erases any existing content?
questions.exp: w+ truncates the file and allows reading and writing; r+ keeps content and a+ appends.

questions.q: In the three-layer architecture of the Internet of Things, which layer is responsible for sensing physical quantities and identifying objects?
questions.exp: The perception (sensing) layer contains sensors, actuators and tags that collect data from the physical world.

questions.q: Which technology characterised the third generation of computers?
questions.exp: Third generation computers (1960s) used integrated circuits; transistors were second generation and vacuum tubes first.

questions.q: An ideal 5-stage pipeline (no stalls) executes 100 instructions. How many clock cycles are needed in total?
What is the subnet mask corresponding to a /26 prefix?
questions.exp: /26 means 26 network bits: 24 bits + 2 bits of the last octet = 11000000 = 192, so 255.255.255.192.

questions.q: In a JK flip-flop, which input combination makes the output toggle on every clock pulse?
questions.exp: With J = K = 1 the characteristic equation Q+ = JQ' + K'Q becomes Q+ = Q', i.e. the output toggles.

questions.q: Which CPU register always holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched from memory?
questions.exp: The Program Counter (PC) stores the address of the next instruction and is updated after each fetch.

questions.q: Under the IT Act 2000 (as amended in 2008), which section deals with punishment for identity theft?
questions.exp: Section 66C punishes fraudulent or dishonest use of another person's password, digital signature or unique identification feature.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
d = {'a': 1, 'b': 2}
d['c'] = d.get('c', 0) + 5
d.update({'a': 10})
print(d)
questions.exp: get returns 0 for missing 'c' so c becomes 5; update overwrites 'a' with 10.

questions.q: Relation R has 5 tuples and relation S has 4 tuples. How many tuples are there in R × S?
questions.exp: Cartesian product pairs every tuple of R with every tuple of S: 5 × 4 = 20.

questions.q: In a star topology with a central hub, the failure of which component brings down the entire network?
questions.exp: All traffic passes through the hub, so hub failure is a single point of failure for the whole network.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of comparisons needed to merge two sorted lists of sizes m and n into one sorted list?
questions.exp: Each comparison outputs one element; the last element is placed without comparison, so at most m + n − 1 comparisons.

questions.q: Which of the following is a document-oriented NoSQL database?
questions.exp: MongoDB stores data as JSON-like (BSON) documents; Redis is key-value, Neo4j is a graph database and HBase is column-family.

questions.q: Which HTML5 element represents self-contained content, such as a news story or blog post, that could be distributed independently?
questions.exp: <article> is the semantic element for independent, self-contained content.

questions.q: Relation R(A, B, C) satisfies the functional dependencies A → B and B → C, and A is the only candidate key. The highest normal form of R is
questions.exp: The key is a single attribute so no partial dependency exists (2NF), but B → C is a transitive dependency of a non-prime attribute, so R is not in 3NF.

questions.q: The Turing test, proposed by Alan Turing in 1950, is designed to check whether a machine can
options: solve any mathematical problem in polynomial time
store more data than a human brain
process images faster than a human
exhibit conversational behaviour indistinguishable from that of a human
questions.exp: In the imitation game a human judge cannot reliably tell the machine from a human through conversation.

questions.q: The function F(A, B, C) = Σm(1, 3, 5, 7) simplifies to
questions.exp: The four minterms are exactly the cells where C = 1, so one quad gives F = C.

questions.q: What is the length of a longest common subsequence of X = ABCBDAB and Y = BDCABA?
questions.exp: One LCS is BCBA (also BDAB); no common subsequence of length 5 exists, so the length is 4.

questions.q: The ACID property that guarantees that once a transaction has committed its changes survive system crashes is
questions.exp: Durability means committed updates persist even after failures, usually via logging to stable storage.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of compile-time (static) polymorphism?
options: Overriding a method of an abstract class
questions.exp: Overloaded calls are resolved by the compiler from the argument list; overriding is resolved at run time.

questions.q: An NFA has 5 states. In the worst case, how many states can the equivalent DFA obtained by subset construction have?
questions.exp: Subset construction can produce up to 2^n states; 2^5 = 32.

questions.q: Which of the following function headers is syntactically INVALID in Python 3?
questions.exp: A parameter without a default value cannot follow a parameter that has a default.

questions.q: A classifier produces TP = 40, FP = 10, FN = 20 and TN = 30. What is its precision?
questions.exp: Precision = TP/(TP+FP) = 40/50 = 0.80.

questions.q: A full adder has inputs A = 1, B = 1 and Cin = 1. The Sum and Carry outputs are
questions.exp: 1 + 1 + 1 = 11 in binary, so Sum = 1 and Carry = 1.

questions.q: In MS Word, which shortcut key opens the Find and Replace dialog box with the Replace tab active?
questions.exp: Ctrl+H opens Replace; Ctrl+F opens Find/Navigation, Ctrl+R right-aligns and Ctrl+P prints.

questions.q: In DMA, the mode in which the DMA controller takes over the bus for just one memory cycle at a time and then returns it to the CPU is called
questions.exp: In cycle stealing the DMA controller steals single bus cycles from the CPU between its own accesses.
Integer division 10/3 = 3 and the remainder 10%3 = 1.

questions.q: The 8255 Programmable Peripheral Interface provides how many programmable I/O lines?
questions.exp: It has three 8-bit ports (A, B, C), giving 24 I/O lines; the chip itself has 40 pins.

questions.q: Which of the following strings does NOT belong to the language of the regular expression (a+b)*abb?
questions.exp: Every string in the language must end with abb; abbb ends with bbb.

questions.q: Which multiplexing technique combines several optical signals of different wavelengths onto a single optical fibre?
questions.exp: Wavelength Division Multiplexing assigns each signal its own light wavelength on the same fibre.

questions.q: How many distinct solutions does the 6-queens problem have?
questions.exp: The 6×6 board admits exactly 4 non-attacking arrangements of 6 queens.

questions.q: In the instruction ADD R1, #25, the second operand is specified using which addressing mode?
questions.exp: The '#' indicates that the constant 25 is part of the instruction itself, which is immediate addressing.

questions.q: What is the result of typeof null in JavaScript?
questions.exp: typeof null returns "object"; this is a long-standing quirk of the language.

questions.q: A circular queue is implemented in an array of size 6 (indices 0 to 5). Front = 4 and rear = 1, where rear is the index of the last inserted element. How many elements are in the queue?
questions.exp: Count = (rear - front + size) mod size + 1 = (1 - 4 + 6) mod 6 + 1 = 3 + 1 = 4 (elements at indices 4, 5, 0, 1).

questions.q: The solution of the recurrence T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n with T(1) = 1 is
questions.exp: Master theorem: a=2, b=2, n^(log₂2) = n equals f(n), so T(n) = Θ(n log n).

questions.q: How many flags are present in the flag register of the 8085 microprocessor?
questions.exp: The 8085 has five flags: Sign, Zero, Auxiliary Carry, Parity and Carry.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a requirement for a solution to the critical-section problem?
questions.exp: The three requirements are mutual exclusion, progress and bounded waiting.

questions.q: In an ER diagram, an attribute that can hold more than one value for a single entity (for example, several phone numbers of one person) is called a
questions.exp: An attribute that can store a set of values for one entity is multivalued; it is drawn with a double ellipse.

questions.q: The halting problem for Turing machines is
questions.exp: A universal TM can simulate M on w and accept if it halts, so the language is RE, but no TM decides it for all inputs.

questions.q: A full binary tree (every node has 0 or 2 children) has 5 internal nodes. What is the total number of nodes in the tree?
questions.exp: In a full binary tree, leaves = internal nodes + 1 = 6, so total = 5 + 6 = 11.

questions.q: A microprocessor with 16 address lines can directly address a memory of
questions.exp: 2^16 = 65,536 locations = 64 KB.

questions.q: In the relational model, a foreign key is
options: an attribute that is unique and never NULL in its own relation
any attribute that appears in more than one relation
an attribute (or set) in one relation that refers to the primary key of another (or the same) relation
the attribute chosen to sort tuples physically
questions.exp: A foreign key references a candidate/primary key of a referenced relation and enforces referential integrity.

questions.q: A direct-mapped cache has a total capacity of 4 KB and a block size of 16 bytes. How many cache lines does it have?
questions.exp: Number of lines = 4096 / 16 = 256.

questions.q: Which type of coupling between two modules is the most undesirable (highest degree of coupling)?
questions.exp: Content coupling, where one module directly modifies or relies on the internals of another, is the strongest and worst form of coupling.

questions.q: In a singly linked list that has only a head pointer, which of the following operations takes O(n) time?
options: Inserting a node at the beginning
Checking whether the list is empty
questions.exp: To delete the last node we must traverse to the second last node, which needs O(n) time; the other operations are O(1).

questions.q: Which of the following is a valid identifier in C?
questions.exp: An identifier must start with a letter or underscore and contain only letters, digits and underscores; 'int' is a keyword.

questions.q: Which UML diagram is used to show the interaction between objects arranged in time order?
questions.exp: A sequence diagram shows messages exchanged between objects along a vertical time axis.

questions.q: The grammar S → aSb | ε generates which language?
options: {w ∈ {a,b}* | w has equal number of a's and b's}
questions.exp: Each application of S → aSb adds one a on the left and one b on the right, so strings are a^n b^n.

questions.q: Which SDLC model is most suitable when the requirements are clearly understood and fixed in advance, and each phase must be completed before the next one begins?
questions.exp: The Waterfall model is a linear sequential model that works best for stable, well-understood requirements.

questions.q: Which statement about a B+ tree is correct?
options: Data records are stored only in the root node
Every internal node stores the data pointers for all its keys
The tree is always a binary tree
All keys with their data pointers appear in the leaf nodes, which are linked to support range scans
questions.exp: In a B+ tree, all search keys with data pointers are in the leaves, and leaves are chained in sequence, making range queries efficient.

questions.q: Which HTTP status code indicates that a new resource has been successfully created, typically in response to a POST request?
questions.exp: 201 Created is returned when a request results in a new resource being created.

questions.q: The command chmod 754 file sets the permissions to:
questions.exp: 7 = rwx for owner, 5 = r-x for group, 4 = r-- for others.

questions.q: A hospital's patient records are secretly modified by an unauthorised person. Which principle of the CIA triad is violated?
questions.exp: Unauthorised modification of data violates integrity, which ensures data stays accurate and unaltered.

questions.q:
Statement I: Depth First Search of a graph can be implemented using a stack.
Statement II: Breadth First Search finds the shortest path (fewest edges) from the source in an unweighted graph.
Which option is correct?
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.exp: DFS uses an explicit or recursion stack, and BFS explores vertices level by level, so it gives fewest-edge paths.

questions.q: Which port of the 8051 microcontroller needs external pull-up resistors when used as a general-purpose I/O port?
questions.exp: Port 0 has open-drain outputs, so external pull-ups are needed for ordinary I/O use.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a necessary condition for deadlock?
options: Resource preemption (resources can be forcibly taken away)
questions.exp: The four Coffman conditions are mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption and circular wait; allowing preemption breaks deadlock.

questions.q: Which of the following is a typical embedded application of a microcontroller?
questions.exp: A washing machine controller is a dedicated, low-cost control task, which is what microcontrollers are designed for.

questions.q: Which malware spreads across a network by copying itself, without needing a host file or any user action?
questions.exp: A worm is self-replicating and standalone; a virus needs a host file and a trojan does not replicate.

questions.q: A system has 32-bit logical addresses and 4 KB pages. How many bits are used for the page number?
questions.exp: 4 KB = 2^12, so the offset is 12 bits and the page number is 32 - 12 = 20 bits.

questions.q: Which data structure is used by the Breadth-First Search (BFS) algorithm to keep track of the nodes to be explored?
questions.exp: BFS explores nodes level by level, so it needs a FIFO queue.

questions.q: A hash table of size 7 uses h(k) = k mod 7 with linear probing. Keys 15, 22, 8 and 29 are inserted in this order. In which slot does 29 finally get stored?
questions.exp: All four keys hash to slot 1. 15 goes to 1, 22 to 2, 8 to 3 and 29 to 4.

questions.q: How many bits are there in 2 KB, taking 1 KB = 1024 bytes?
Guilford regarded creativity as closely related to
questions.exp: Divergent thinking produces many different ideas for open-ended problems.

questions.q: The word 'curriculum' is derived from the Latin word 'currere', which means:
options: to run a race or course
questions.exp: Curriculum originally meant a race course or track to be run.

questions.q: G. Stanley Hall described adolescence as a period of
questions.exp: Hall regarded adolescence as a turbulent period with emotional ups and downs.

questions.q: Erikson's theory of development is known as the
questions.exp: Erikson described eight stages of psychosocial crises over the life span.

questions.q: The formula for the intelligence quotient is
questions.exp: Intelligence quotient = MA/CA × 100.

questions.q: Microteaching was first developed at:
questions.exp: Dwight Allen and colleagues developed it at Stanford in the early 1960s.

questions.q: The project method of teaching was popularised by:
questions.exp: Kilpatrick developed the project method on the basis of John Dewey's philosophy.

questions.q: In Edgar Dale's Cone of Experience, the base of the cone (most concrete) is:
questions.exp: Dale placed direct experience at the bottom and verbal symbols at the top.

questions.q: At the base of Maslow's hierarchy of needs lie the
questions.exp: Basic needs such as food, water and sleep must be satisfied first.

questions.q: Frank Parsons is known as the father of
questions.exp: Parsons founded the Vocation Bureau in 1908.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most important quality of a good teacher?
questions.exp: Understanding learners together with command of the subject makes teaching effective.

questions.q: The main purpose of a diagnostic test is to:
options: identify the specific weaknesses of learners and their causes
questions.exp: Diagnostic testing locates learning difficulties for remediation.

questions.q: A child with IQ 130 or above is generally termed
questions.exp: IQ above about 130 is commonly considered gifted.

questions.q: In Herbart's five formal steps, the step that follows 'presentation' is:
questions.exp: The order is preparation, presentation, comparison (association), generalisation, application.

questions.q: A blueprint of a question paper is a:
options: three-dimensional chart showing weightage to objectives, content and question forms
questions.exp: The blueprint ensures balanced coverage of objectives, content and types of questions.

questions.q: Individual differences among students are caused by
questions.exp: Both inherited and environmental factors produce variation.

questions.q: Allport defined personality as the dynamic organisation within the individual of
options: those psychophysical systems that determine his unique adjustment to the environment
questions.exp: This is Allport's classic definition.

questions.q: Vygotsky's 'Zone of Proximal Development' is the gap between
options: what a child can do alone and what the child can do with guidance
a child's mental age and chronological age
questions.exp: ZPD lies between independent performance and the level reachable with help from a more capable person.

questions.q: The school structure proposed in NEP 2020 is:
questions.exp: The 5+3+3+4 design replaces the earlier 10+2 structure.

questions.q: Thorndike's 'Law of Effect' states that
options: responses followed by satisfying consequences are strengthened
questions.exp: Satisfying outcomes stamp in a stimulus-response connection.

questions.q: In Pavlov's experiment, the sound of the bell before conditioning is a
questions.exp: Before pairing with food, the bell does not cause salivation, so it is neutral.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a core element of computational thinking?
questions.exp: The core elements are decomposition, pattern recognition, abstraction and algorithm design.

questions.q: Kohlberg's theory of moral development is based on
options: moral behaviour observed in daily life
moral reasoning given in response to dilemmas
questions.exp: Kohlberg analysed the reasons people gave for solving dilemmas such as the Heinz dilemma.

questions.q: SWAYAM is:
options: a social media site only for teachers
a national platform that offers free online courses (MOOCs) to learners in India
questions.exp: SWAYAM is the Government of India MOOC platform from the Ministry of Education.

questions.q: The validity of a test refers to:
options: the extent to which it measures what it is meant to measure
questions.exp: A valid test measures the intended attribute.

questions.q: According to John Adams, teaching is a bipolar process. The two poles are:
questions.exp: Adams viewed teaching as a face-to-face interaction between the teacher and the learner.

questions.q: In educational psychology, the term 'growth' mainly refers to
options: qualitative changes in behaviour and skills
changes in personality due to training
quantitative physical changes such as increase in height and weight
questions.exp: Growth is the measurable, quantitative increase in size, height and weight; development is qualitative and wider.

questions.q: Formative assessment is conducted:
options: only at the end of the year
during the learning process to improve teaching and learning
questions.exp: It gives continuous feedback, so that gaps can be corrected immediately.

questions.q: The term 'action research' was first used by:
questions.exp: Kurt Lewin introduced the term in the 1940s.

questions.q: According to Piaget, the first stage of cognitive development is the
questions.exp: Piaget's stages in order are sensorimotor, preoperational, concrete operational and formal operational.

questions.q: Who presided over the first session of the Indian National Congress held in Bombay in 1885?
questions.exp: The first INC session (1885, Bombay) was presided over by W. C. Bonnerjee; A. O. Hume was its founder-organiser.

questions.q: Which is the longest river that flows entirely within India?
questions.exp: The Ganga (about 2,525 km) is the longest river wholly in India; Brahmaputra and Indus rise outside India.

questions.q: Which modern city of Bihar was the ancient Mauryan capital Pataliputra?
questions.exp: Pataliputra, capital of the Magadha-Mauryan empire, is the modern city of Patna.

questions.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution abolishes untouchability?

questions.q: What is the SI unit of electric charge?
questions.exp: Electric charge is measured in coulomb (1 C = 1 A x 1 s); ampere is the unit of current.

questions.q: The scientific study of the relationship between living organisms and their physical environment is called
questions.exp: Ecology (term coined by Ernst Haeckel) studies organisms and their interactions with the environment.

questions.q: In the food chain Grass → Grasshopper → Frog → Snake → Hawk, which organism is the secondary consumer?
questions.exp: Grasshopper is the primary consumer; frog, which eats it, is the secondary consumer.

questions.q: The Montreal Protocol (1987) was adopted to control the production and use of
questions.exp: The Montreal Protocol phases out substances such as CFCs and halons that deplete the ozone layer.

questions.q: The Chipko Movement, which involved hugging trees to prevent felling, began in the 1970s in which present-day state?
questions.exp: Chipko began in Chamoli district (now Uttarakhand); Sunderlal Bahuguna and Gaura Devi are associated with it.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a greenhouse gas?
questions.exp: Greenhouse gases absorb infrared radiation; molecular nitrogen does not.

questions.q: Pointing to a man, Rina said, 'He is the son of my mother's only brother.' How is the man related to Rina?
questions.exp: Rina's mother's brother is her maternal uncle; his son is Rina's cousin.

questions.q: A man walks 6 km towards north, turns right and walks 8 km, then turns right again and walks 6 km. How far and in which direction is he from the starting point?
questions.exp: North 6, then east 8, then south 6 cancels the north-south displacement, leaving 8 km east of the start.

questions.q:
Statements: All pens are books. Some books are tables.
Conclusions: I. Some pens are tables. II. Some tables are books.
questions.exp: Some books are tables implies some tables are books (II). The pens-tables link is not established since the books that are tables may not be pens, so I does not follow.
